report.clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man presents with a painless neck lump persisting for about two months and increased fatigue after work. He attributes the fatigue to aging and a busy life, and the lump initially to stress-related swollen lymph nodes. He has no recent infections or dental appointments. His father had chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) in remission for nearly five years, managed with watch-and-wait. The patient maintains a healthy lifestyle, gets blood tests every three months due to family history, and trusts the clinician's judgment. He is open to physical examination and further tests if needed.

evidence.quote: The fatigue is definitely affecting me more than usual though. It's not as bad as feeling sick all the time, but it feels like a low-level exhaustion that doesn't seem to go away even when I get good rest at night.
I've been putting it down to getting older and maybe just having a busy life in general.
